target.title: fix: tasks.list re-sorts the whole registry on every Control UI poll
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI's `tasks.list` poll stalls the gateway event loop on busy installs. Each call cloned and O(n log n) sorted every task record by `createdAt`, then immediately re-sorted the filtered set by last activity and sliced a bounded page — so the `createdAt` sort was thrown away, and the full re-sort ran across the entire registry on every poll. On gateways with thousands of accumulated completed/failed tasks this produced a noticeable event-loop stall per RPC (#101716).

Closes #101716.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes remove the wasted work while keeping the wire output byte-for-byte identical:

1. **Skip the discarded `createdAt` sort.** A new `listTaskRecordsUnsorted()` returns cloned records without the registry's newest-created sort (and the `insertionIndex` bookkeeping that only exists to support it). The `tasks.list` handler re-sorts by last activity anyway, so the registry sort was pure waste.
2. **Only sort the window the client needs.** `partialSortTopK` quickselects the `cursor + limit` window and fully sorts just that window — O(n + k log k) instead of O(n log n) — with a full-sort fallback when `k >= n`.

The page comparator (`taskUpdatedAt` desc, `taskId` asc) is unchanged, and since `taskId` is unique the order is a total order, so quickselect's non-stability cannot change results.

## User Impact

Operators of busy gateways get snappier Control UI task-list polling and no per-poll event-loop stalls as the task registry grows over days of uptime. Paging behavior and ordering are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` → **9 passed**.
- New pagination test (pages past the first page) and a new equivalence test that pages through 12 records with mixed distinct/duplicate `lastEventAt` values and asserts the collected order across all pages exactly matches a full-sort reference — exercising both the partial-sort (`k < n`) path and the full-sort (`k >= n`) path, plus the `taskId` tie-break. Repeated 6× to confirm the randomized quickselect pivot is not flaky.
- `oxlint` clean; `tsgo:test:src` (test typecheck) clean.

## Notes

This combines and completes two earlier partial attempts (both still open with failing checks):
- #102132 added `listTaskRecordsUnsorted()` but left the full handler re-sort in place (`check-test-types` failed).
- #102118 added `partialSortTopK` but still called the sorted `listTaskRecords()` (`check-lint` failed).

This PR takes both ideas, resolves both CI failures, and adds the equivalence regression neither had. Happy to rework or fold into one of those if a maintainer prefers.
